idea.name: Sushi restaurant chain
idea.one_liner: A proposed sushi chain for diners, intended to scale like fast-casual chains; restaurant sales are implied, but no unit economics are given.
idea.offer: Sushi served through a restaurant chain
idea.revenue_model: Restaurant sales implied; not stated explicitly

key_quotes.quote: And me and my two buddies have had this brilliant idea to start a new restaurant concept.
We think we're going to be the next Chipotle, the next subway, the next five guys. And we're going to do it in the world of sushi.
The last thing you want to do is a founder is build something that nobody wants.
The better way is to validate your idea as you go earlier, the better.
saying we're going to open the doors in the next 90 days and getting going and start serving customers and start figuring out how to make them happy.
We're no closer to the restaurant than we were five months ago. We've just been wasting our time with this plan.

claims.claim: The host says he and two friends co-founded the restaurant concept, making three founders.
claims.quote: And me and my two buddies have had this brilliant idea to start a new restaurant concept.

claims.claim: The host says he had tried sushi about three or five months before the idea.
claims.quote: In fact, before I had this idea, before this moment of embarrassment, I had really tried sushi like three months prior or five months prior or something like that.

claims.claim: The host says he spent three months working on bringing the business to life.
claims.quote: For the last three months before this, I had been working on bringing this business to life.

claims.claim: The team printed a business plan described as 250 pages.
claims.quote: We printed out this binder, it was like this thick and I think it's like a 250 page business plan

claims.claim: The host later describes the binder as 300 pages, conflicting with his earlier 250-page description.
claims.quote: pretty quickly, he's just trying to rock like what the hell could possibly be in this 300 page binder.

claims.claim: The restaurant founder advised opening within 90 days of securing a location and lease.
claims.quote: saying we're going to open the doors in the next 90 days and getting going and start serving customers and start figuring out how to make them happy.

claims.claim: The team was no closer to the restaurant after five months of planning.
claims.quote: We're no closer to the restaurant than we were five months ago.

claims.claim: The team returned to a mentor 48 hours after receiving advice.
claims.quote: And like 48 hours later, we came back to him and we're like, cool.

claims.claim: The team repeated that follow-up process three times with the mentor.
claims.quote: And we just did that like three times with him and then he wrote this blog post for the world to see it.

claims.claim: The host says the action-oriented approach served him a year later.
claims.quote: And that really served me a year later.

ideas.delivery: The founders intended to secure restaurant premises, lease a location, open, and serve diners. The transcript says the concept remained at the planning stage and does not say it launched.
ideas.other_uk_rules: UK food safety and allergen-information rules would apply to restaurants; the transcript gives no compliance details.

idea.name: My First Million podcast
idea.one_liner: A host-led show for listeners, intended to entertain and share insight; monetization is not stated.
idea.offer: Storytelling and guest-led podcast episodes intended to entertain and provide insight

key_quotes.quote: Hey man, listen to your podcast. You know, you do a good job. But you want to be great at podcasting, right? This is like your thing.
Because you're saying like all the time, you say like 500 times in an episode.
I think I could say things that will entertain people and will contain enough insight that to walk away and being like, I kind of want to listen to that guy again.
And so I created a show and I booked a studio and I got my friend to be my first guest and that became episode one of my first million.

claims.claim: Scott Harrison estimated that the host said “like” 500 times in an episode of his podcast.
claims.quote: Because you're saying like all the time, you say like 500 times in an episode.

claims.claim: The host says he created the show with a first guest and that became episode one.
claims.quote: And so I created a show and I booked a studio and I got my friend to be my first guest and that became episode one of my first million.
